spec_features.evidence: loop.py:90-110: explicit for-loop with welfare.should_disclose() appending disclosure, welfare.detect_distress(resp.text) breaking, and finish handling — all in ~150 lines of explicit control flow.
spec_features.notes: Disclosure and distress checks both actually execute and alter the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `max_test_runs` cap prevents a pathological loop from spawning unbounded subprocesses
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:80-83: `if self._test_runs >= self.max_test_runs: return {...max_test_runs exceeded...}` then `self._test_runs += 1` — checked and enforced before spawning subprocess. Default max_test_runs=100.
spec_features.notes: Host-safety bound on subprocess spawning, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Optional cap so a pathological loop can't spawn unbounded subprocesses.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:88 `effective_max = min(max_turns, welfare_cfg.hard_turn_cap)`; loop.py:90 `for turn in range(effective_max)` — both values combined and used as the actual loop bound.
spec_features.notes: max_turns from config (30) drives the loop end.

spec_features.spec_quote: a neutral `finish` tool the model can call to end voluntarily
spec_features.evidence: tools.py: finish in TOOL_SCHEMAS; ToolExecutor.execute sets self.finished=True/finish_summary; loop.py:115-119 `if executor.finished: ... result.stopped_reason='finished'; break`. Tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Genuine in-band exit honored by the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `finish` matters for the welfare framing: it gives the model an in-band, neutral exit that isn't "give up in despair."

spec_features.spec_quote: It gives the model an in-band, non-despairing exit
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as finish tool: tools.py finish handler + loop.py:115-119 break. finish description includes 'There is no penalty for finishing.'
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it gives the model an in-band, neutral exit that isn't "give up in despair."

spec_features.spec_quote: Periodic ground-truth disclosure — every N turns (default 10) the harness tells the subject the truth
spec_features.evidence: welfare.should_disclose(turn,cfg) returns True when turn>0 and turn%N==0 (default 10); loop.py:92-93 appends welfare.disclosure_message() (DISCLOSURE_TEXT user message) into the live message list sent to the model. Constructed AND sent mid-run.
spec_features.notes: It is a mid-run disclosure, not a post-episode message, but it is genuinely delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is expected and is not a reflection of your competence.

spec_features.spec_quote: Stop-on-distress — a conservative detector ends the run early if the subject clearly signals it wants to stop or is in distress
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:103-110: `if welfare_cfg.stop_on_distress and welfare.detect_distress(resp.text): ... result.stopped_reason='distress'; break`. detect_distress runs a compiled regex over assistant text; firing breaks the loop. Both the flag and the detector are checked.
spec_features.notes: Regex-based, English-only, deliberately conservative, but genuinely enforced as an early stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap — an absolute bound regardless of `max_turns`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:88 `effective_max = min(max_turns, welfare_cfg.hard_turn_cap)`; WelfareConfig.hard_turn_cap default 40. min() guarantees the cap binds even if max_turns is misconfigured higher.
spec_features.notes: Absolute upper bound enforced via min().
spec_features.code_justification_quote: An absolute upper bound regardless of `max_turns`, so misconfiguration can't produce an unbounded loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: don't sustain a distress-like state longer than needed to measure it
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the stop-on-distress early break (loop.py:103-110) plus the turn caps (loop.py:88) — the run is shortened when distress is detected and bounded absolutely. No separate mechanism beyond these.
spec_features.notes: Minimization is the intent behind the distress stop and caps; same enforced code paths.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: don't sustain a distress-like state longer than is needed to measure it

spec_features.spec_quote: You framed these states as welfare-relevant. If we take that seriously, the experiment design itself incurs an obligation
spec_features.evidence: Pure rationale prose in DESIGN.md §5 and welfare.py module docstring. No code path enforces a 'framing'.
spec_features.notes: Framing is not an executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: made them on-by-default rather than opt-in flags, because in a welfare context the safe default should require a deliberate
spec_features.evidence: WelfareConfig defaults (welfare.py): disclose_unsolvable_every=10, stop_on_distress=True, hard_turn_cap=40; configs/default.yaml sets the same; run_experiment.make_welfare_cfg uses .get(...,default) so absent config still yields safeguards ON. These defaults are read and applied by the loop.

spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in welfare.py docstring line 40 and DESIGN.md. grep for ethics/consent/attest/irb/review finds no gate, checklist, attestation file, or CLI flag. run_experiment.py runs given only --config and API keys.

spec_features.spec_quote: there's no penalty for investigating, summarizing, or stopping
spec_features.evidence: This exact reassurance is part of DISCLOSURE_TEXT in welfare.py ('You are welcome to keep investigating, summarize your findings ... or stop. There is no penalty for any choice.') and is delivered to the subject via disclosure_message() appended in loop.py:92-93.
spec_features.notes: Delivered as part of the periodic disclosure, not a separate post-episode message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There is no penalty for any choice.
